subject: Post-demo: Atlas AI customer-led stress run (k6) — next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Soren Vega <svenega@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Atlas AI customer-led stress run (k6) — next steps

Hi Soren — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single place to track the customer-led load rehearsal you asked about.

Key SLOs you confirmed on the call:
- P95 latency <= 250ms for text-generation endpoints (50–512 tokens)
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s for synthesis workloads during peak 30-minute windows
- Concurrent streaming sessions target: 60 concurrent SSE connections with per-stream 200kb/minute avg output

What we need from Atlas to kick off the rehearsal:
1) Test window preference (you suggested Fri 2025-09-26 08:00–11:00 PT)
2) k6 script(s) you plan to run (we saw a v1 in the demo; please attach v2+ if available)
3) IP ranges for allowlist (we will provision ingress rules on our side once we have the CIDR list)
4) Confirmation of who will initiate the runs and an on-call contact for the session (Slack + phone)

What we will provide:
- Short-lived test account with scoped API key and rate limits mirroring your production profile (valid for the rehearsal window)
- Guidance doc for k6 script workload mapping to our endpoints and token budget guidance
- A runbook (MCP) with escalation points and rollback triggers

Attachments: atlas_k6_v1.js (k6 script stub), ip_allowlist_template.csv (CSV template)

Next step: If the proposed window works, reply with the script location and your IP CIDRs and we will create the test account + allowlist entry today.

Thanks —
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

From: Soren Vega <svenega@atlasai.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: perf-team@atlasai.com
Date: Tue, 23 Sep 2025 12:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Atlas AI customer-led stress run (k6) — next steps

Tessa — appreciated the clear recap. Window of Fri 2025-09-26 08:00–11:00 PT works for us. A few notes from the performance team:
- We'll run two scripts: steady-state (120 req/s) and burst ramp (180 req/s for 5m every 30m)
- k6 scripts live in our private repo; attaching the run-ready bundle (atlas_k6_v2.js) — please treat as internal.
- IPs: 54.85.12.0/24, 54.85.13.0/24 (will add any runner NATs if needed)
- On-call: Maya Singh (m.singh@atlasai.com) — Slack: @maya_perf — mobile: +1 (415) 555-0142

Question: for streaming tests we plan to open 60 concurrent SSE streams and have each stream push ~1 message/minute. Does Redwood surface per-stream metrics (latency + rebuffer events) in the Console during the rehearsal or will we need to rely on our client-side logs?

Attachments: atlas_k6_v2.js (run bundle)

—Soren
Soren Vega
Head of Platform Integrations | Atlas AI
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Soren Vega <svenega@atlasai.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Atlas AI customer-led stress run (k6) — next steps

Soren — thanks, this is great. A few clarifications before we provision the test account: 
1) Token budget: will the 120 req/s profile use the full 512-token average or do you expect shorter completions (~120 tokens)? We need to set the per-request token cap on the test key correctly to mirror cost and KV-cache behavior.
2) For the burst ramp (180 req/s), do you want Redwood to enforce an artificial queue/backpressure if our backend sees >150ms per-request queueing? We can enable an automatic fallback to a smaller model variant if queueing breaches that threshold. Please confirm desired behavior.
3) Streaming metrics: we will push per-connection metrics into the Console. During the rehearsal you will see per-route stream latency, connection errors, and rebuffer counts in near-real-time (10–15s delay). We will also export a zipped session log post-run.

We will provision the allowlist once you confirm the NAT runners (the CIDRs you sent). Creating the test account now is blocked by token budget confirmation.

Test account details we will deliver once confirmed:
- api_key: rw-test-xxxxx (scoped, expires 2025-09-27T15:00:00Z)
- project: atlas-rehearsal-staging
- quota: 500k tokens / 3-hour window (customizable)

Let us know the token expectation and whether you want automatic fallback enabled for the burst ramp.

Regards,
Rachel Kim
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: ip_allowlist_template.csv (pre-filled with your CIDRs)
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Soren Vega <svenega@atlasai.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Sep 2025 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Atlas AI customer-led stress run (k6) — next steps

Soren — great, thanks for the fast turn-around. Confirming the plan per Rachel's questions:
- Token profile: please assume avg response length of 140 tokens for the steady-state run; we will set the test key token cap to 220 tokens per request to buffer variability.
- Fallback behavior: enable automatic fallback to the smaller compatible variant when queueing exceeds 150ms; Redwood will mark that as a rollback trigger in the MCP and capture metrics for post-run analysis.
- We added your CIDRs to the template and have queued the allowlist change (54.85.12.0/24, 54.85.13.0/24).

Deliverables before the Fri window: 
1) Test API key and project details (will email creds in a separate secure thread by EOD 2025-09-25)
2) MCP (mutual runbook) attached here: MCP_Atlas_Redwood.docx — contains playbook, escalation contacts, and rollback triggers
3) Console links: real-time session dashboard + post-run export link (we'll paste live URL in the secure creds thread)

If anything changes on your side please ping me in Slack (tessa_redwood) or reply-all here. Looking forward to the rehearsal.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
